chunks: From him, from Zakariyya ibn Muhammad, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man comes to me with dinars, wanting dirhams from me, so I give him the cheapest [rate] compared to what I sell [at]. He said: 'Give him the cheapest [rate] that you find for him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended exchange rate when selling gold for silver in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *fadl* (excess) in currency exchange, instructing the seller to offer the most favorable rate to the buyer to ensure equity. In Shia jurisprudence, this reflects the broader ethical imperative of avoiding exploitation in *sarf* (gold for silver) transactions, where the hand-to-hand exchange must be equal in weight and free from hidden usury. The ruling underscores the Imam’s emphasis on commercial justice, ensuring that the party with the commodity (gold) does not disadvantage the party seeking liquidity (silver).
